tasks.title: Implement ngv2/confidence.py — 4-tier confidence scoring from multi-tool agreement
acceptance_criteria: A new single file ngv2/confidence.py is created (whole-file authoring, no edits to other files).
The module exposes a top-level CONFIDENCE_TIERS object defining exactly 4 confidence tiers in a fixed, deterministic order.
The module exposes a callable classify(signals) that maps multi-tool agreement signals to exactly one of the 4 tiers defined in CONFIDENCE_TIERS.
classify is pure and deterministic: identical inputs always yield identical outputs, with no randomness, wall-clock, or environment dependence.
The module imports only the Python standard library; no third-party imports and no file/network I/O.
The command `python -m pytest tests/test_confidence.py -q` passes against the already-committed oracle without modifying that oracle.
No new test files are authored or modified; tests/test_confidence.py remains untouched.

spec.objective: Author a new, single-file, pure/deterministic, stdlib-only Python module ngv2/confidence.py that provides multi-tool confidence scoring by exposing CONFIDENCE_TIERS (the ordered definition of the 4 confidence tiers) and classify(signals) (a deterministic mapping from multi-tool agreement signals to one of those 4 tiers). The committed oracle tests/test_confidence.py is the sole source of truth for the exact tier names/order and classify semantics.
functional_requirements: Define and expose CONFIDENCE_TIERS as a top-level, ordered definition of exactly four confidence tiers, with names/values and ordering matching exactly what tests/test_confidence.py pins.
Define and expose classify(signals) as a top-level callable that accepts the multi-tool agreement signals shape required by the oracle and returns one of the four tiers defined in CONFIDENCE_TIERS.
Implement the agreement-to-tier mapping so that the degree of multi-tool agreement deterministically selects the tier exactly as specified by the oracle's expected (input, tier) pairs.

Guarantee determinism: classify(signals) is a pure function of its argument(s) with no use of randomness, wall-clock time, or environment/OS state, so repeated calls on equal inputs return equal results.
Restrict the module to the Python standard library only — no third-party imports — and perform no file or network I/O at import time or call time.

Handle the boundary/degenerate signal inputs covered by the oracle (e.g. no agreement / single tool / partial agreement / full agreement) by routing each to its pinned tier without raising unless the oracle expects an error.
spec.interfaces: ngv2/confidence.py exposes module-level `CONFIDENCE_TIERS` (the ordered set/definition of the 4 confidence tiers) and `classify(signals)` returning one of the 4 tiers. Exact tier identifiers, ordering, the accepted `signals` shape, and the precise classify mapping are dictated verbatim by the committed oracle tests/test_confidence.py and must be mirrored exactly.
edge_cases: Empty / no-agreement signals (zero supporting tools) must map to the lowest tier as pinned by the oracle.
Single-tool signal must map to its designated low/medium tier rather than a high-agreement tier.
Full multi-tool agreement must map to the highest tier.
Equal inputs presented in different call invocations must yield identical tiers (idempotent/deterministic).
Any malformed/unexpected signal shape should be handled exactly as the oracle expects (either a defined tier or a defined exception type), with no nondeterministic fallback.
non_goals: No nondeterminism: no randomness, wall-clock, or environment dependence.
Do NOT author or modify any test/oracle; tests/test_confidence.py is already committed and is the source of truth.
No dependency on the semgrep_adapter or fp_filter siblings, and no dependency on sibling sub-epics.
No cross-module wiring or integration glue; if any Epic-1/Epic-2 shape is needed it is consumed only via a plain import of an already-tested public symbol.
spec.implementation_notes:
Read tests/test_confidence.py first and treat it as the exact specification: extract the literal tier names and their order to build CONFIDENCE_TIERS, and extract every (signals, expected_tier) assertion to derive the classify mapping (thresholds/comparisons over the count or set of agreeing tools). Prefer a simple, explicit, branch-or-threshold implementation over anything clever so behavior is obviously deterministic. Keep the whole module self-contained: only `from __future__`/stdlib imports if any. Do not add I/O, logging side effects, or global mutable state. Verify locally with `python -m pytest tests/test_confidence.py -q` from working_dir /home/xnihil0zer0/NobleGreedv2; do not edit the oracle to make it pass.

# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/test_confidence.py
```python
"""RED oracle for ngv2.confidence — 4-tier confidence classification from
multi-tool agreement signals. Pure stdlib, deterministic."""
from ngv2.confidence import CONFIDENCE_TIERS, classify


def test_tiers_constant():
    assert CONFIDENCE_TIERS == ('CONFIRMED', 'HIGH', 'MEDIUM', 'LOW')


def test_known_fp_is_low_even_with_signals():
    assert classify({'proof': True, 'tools_agree': 3, 'known_fp': True}) == 'LOW'


def test_proof_is_confirmed():
    # a formal proof (taint flow / PoC run) -> CONFIRMED
    assert classify({'proof': True, 'tools_agree': 0, 'known_fp': False}) == 'CONFIRMED'


def test_multiple_tools_agree_is_high():
    assert classify({'proof': False, 'tools_agree': 2, 'known_fp': False}) == 'HIGH'
    assert classify({'proof': False, 'tools_agree': 5, 'known_fp': False}) == 'HIGH'


def test_single_tool_is_medium():
    assert classify({'proof': False, 'tools_agree': 1, 'known_fp': False}) == 'MEDIUM'


def test_no_signal_is_low():
    assert classify({'proof': False, 'tools_agree': 0, 'known_fp': False}) == 'LOW'
    # missing keys default to no-signal -> LOW
    assert classify({}) == 'LOW'

```
